exercises.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.instructions: Don't go heavy, keep it slow and controlled on the way down. Press straight up, don't flare your elbows too wide.
exercises.description:
1. Sit on a bench with back support or stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
3. Bring your shoulders back, engage your core, and take a breath.
4. Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are fully extended overhead. Exhale at the top.
5. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height — take 3-4 seconds on the way down.
6. Keep the movement smooth and controlled throughout.

exercises.name: Single arm cable lateral raise
exercises.instructions: I love this one, i like to cross my leg over the other and lean away from the cable a bit. Cable stays in front of your body, raise to shoulder height only. Try to focus on leading with your elbow, less so your hand.
exercises.description:
1. Set the cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a single handle.
2. Stand side-on to the machine and grip the handle with the hand furthest from it.
3. Stand tall, core engaged, slight bend in the elbow.
4. Take a breath and raise your arm out to the side until it's parallel to the floor. Exhale at the top.
5. Slowly lower back to the start — don't let the weight stack drop.
6. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

exercises.name: Rear delt reverse fly machine
exercises.instructions: Chest against the pad and squeeze your shoulder blades together at the back, try not to swing your arms cuz then the muscles wont work as hard.
exercises.description:
1. Sit facing the pad on the reverse fly machine, chest pressed lightly against it.
2. Grip the handles with a neutral or pronated grip, arms almost fully extended.
3. Bring your shoulders down and back before you begin.
4. Take a breath and pull the handles outward and back in a wide arc, squeezing your rear delts and rhomboids at the end range.
5. Pause briefly at the back, then slowly return to the start. Breathe in on the way back.
6. Keep your chest on the pad throughout — don't lean back into the movement.

exercises.name: Clamshells
exercises.instructions: Loop a band just above your knees. Keep your hips stacked and feet together, the only thing that moves is your top knee. Try not to let the pelvis rock backwardss.
exercises.description:
1. Loop a resistance band just above your knees.
2. Lie on your side with your hips stacked, knees bent to about 45 degrees, and feet together.
3. Rest your head on your bottom arm and place your top hand on your hip to keep it from rolling back.
4. Engage your core and keep your feet together throughout.
5. Take a breath and rotate your top knee upward like a clamshell opening, squeezing your glute at the top.
6. Slowly lower your knee back to the start. Breathe out as you open.
7. Complete all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: Banded standing glute kickbacks
exercises.instructions: Use a light to medium band. Keep your torso upright and squeeze your glute hard at the top, if you're leaning forward a lot it's probably too tight of a band.
exercises.description:
1. Loop one end of a resistance band around the base of a squat rack at ankle height and the other end around your ankle — or place the band around both ankles if no rack is available.
2. Stand facing the rack and hold it lightly with both hands — just for balance, not to pull on.
3. Stand tall, engage your core, and keep your hips level.
4. Slowly kick the banded leg straight back, squeezing your glute at the top.
5. Don't let your hip hike up or your torso lean forward — that means the back is taking over.
6. Pause at the top, then slowly bring the leg back to start.
7. Complete all reps on one side before switching.
